name: jaffrey lentils
instructions:
Madhur Jaffrey's tarka-style dal — whole green lentils + tomato + asafetida + mustard seeds + dried red chiles + onion + garlic + coriander, finished with chopped fresh cilantro + mint stirred in raw off heat. The mint + cilantro herb pair is the through-line with [[mint-cilantro-skillet]] (chicken/tofu variants) but the technique family here is entirely different — this is a proper tarka dal, not a mortar-pestle herb-sauce-on-protein.

Originally captured as Variant C of the mint-cilantro-skillet file; split into its own recipe because it's structurally its own dish.

SERVES 4. Stovetop, ~40-50 min.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1 tbsp vegetable oil (see notes — tarka wants neutral oil, NOT ghee)
- 1/2 tsp cumin seeds
- 1/2 tsp mustard seeds
- pinch of asafetida
- 1-3 whole dried red chiles
- 1 small yellow onion, sliced in fine half rings
- 2 cloves garlic, chopped
- 1 medium tomato, chopped
- 1 cup whole green lentils
- water to cover (~3 cups)
- 3/4 tsp salt
- 1 tsp ground coriander
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro (added off heat at the end)
- 1/2 cup chopped fresh mint (added off heat at the end)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. BLOOM THE WHOLE SPICES: heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, asafetida, and dried red chiles. Bloom until fragrant and the mustard seeds start to pop (~30-60 seconds).

2. SAUTÉ ONION: add the yellow onion half rings. Sauté until softening (~3-4 min).

3. ADD GARLIC AND TOMATO: stir in the chopped garlic, then the chopped tomato. Cook until the tomato breaks down and the mixture starts to look like a chunky base (~5 min).

4. ADD LENTILS AND WATER: pour in the whole green lentils, water to cover (~3 cups), salt, and ground coriander. Bring to a simmer.

5. SIMMER UNTIL TENDER: reduce heat, cover partially, and simmer until the lentils are tender through — 30-40 min depending on lentil age. Add more water if it dries out too fast; the finished consistency should be moist but not soupy.

6. FINISH WITH HERBS OFF HEAT: remove from heat. Stir in the chopped fresh cilantro and fresh mint. Serve immediately over rice or with flatbread.
notes:
Madhur Jaffrey's tarka-style dal (whole green lentil), finished with the mint + cilantro herb pair that also anchors [[mint-cilantro-skillet]]. Sister recipe by herb pair, unrelated by technique.

=== TARKA-STYLE DAL STRUCTURE ===

This is a proper tarka dal — the technique is: bloom whole spices in neutral oil, then build the base (onion + garlic + tomato), then add lentils and water and simmer. Different structural pattern from ground-spice curries (which cook powdered spices into a masala before adding protein).

The mint + cilantro herb finish is Jaffrey's specific move that ties this recipe to the [[mint-cilantro-skillet]] chicken/tofu variants — but the tarka base + lentil-simmer format has nothing else in common with those. Same herb pair, entirely different cooking pattern.

=== VEGETABLE OIL, NOT GHEE ===

Unlike most indian dishes in the cookbook (which lean ghee-forward), this tarka dal wants NEUTRAL VEGETABLE OIL. Ghee's own character would compete with the mustard-seed-and-asafetida top note that the tarka is built around. 1 tbsp is enough — Jaffrey's original calls for 3 tbsp, which is too much fat for the finished dish. Keep the fat lean here so the whole spices lead.

=== TOMATO AND ASAFETIDA ARE THE LENTIL-SPECIFIC INGREDIENTS ===

Both ingredients are absent from the mint-cilantro-skillet chicken and tofu variants. They belong to the dal pattern here:
- TOMATO (one medium, chopped, into the tarka): breaks down into the base as it cooks with the lentils, adding acid and body.
- ASAFETIDA (a pinch with the whole spices): distinctive sulfurous-oniony note that's classic in indian lentil dishes. Non-optional here.
- MUSTARD SEEDS + DRIED RED CHILES: the tarka whole spices. Popping mustard seeds are what mark this as a proper tarka.

Don't backport these to the mint-cilantro-skillet chicken or tofu variants — they belong to this recipe.

=== NO GINGER, LIME, TURMERIC, OR CHILI POWDER HERE ===

Unlike the [[mint-cilantro-skillet]] chicken/tofu variants, this dal skips:
- GINGER and LIME (those brighten the mortar-pestle herb finish in variants A and B; the mint-cilantro raw-stir-in here doesn't want them)
- TURMERIC and CHILI POWDER (variants A/B use them for a warming spice-crust on the protein; this tarka uses whole dried red chiles + asafetida for a different heat/aromatic axis)

Different chile stack: whole dried red chiles here vs the kashmiri + generic chili powder + red chili flakes combination in the skillet variants.

=== HERBS STIRRED IN AT THE END — NO MORTAR, NO CHIMICHURRI ===

Same don't-cook-the-herbs principle as the [[mint-cilantro-skillet]] chicken/tofu variants, different application. Chopped cilantro + mint go in raw at the finish, off heat. No mortar-pestle work; no chimichurri on the side (see below).

=== NO CHIMICHURRI PAIRING ===

Unlike the mint-cilantro-skillet chicken and tofu variants, [[mint-cilantro-chimichurri]] is NOT appropriate here. The tarka-style dal has its own herbal finish (the raw mint + cilantro stir-in), and the chimichurri's vinegar-and-raw-onion structure would fight the tomato + asafetida base. Skip.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[mint-cilantro-skillet]]: chicken and tofu variants sharing the mint + cilantro herb pair, but built on the priya-krishna mortar-pestle-or-chop herb-finish-on-protein pattern rather than this tarka-style dal pattern. Same herb pair, different technique family.
- [[mint-cilantro-chimichurri]]: NOT appropriate here (see above); belongs with the skillet chicken/tofu variants only.
- Other indian dals / dal-adjacent dishes in the cookbook: [[mediterranean-dal]] (chunky lentil dal, different herb finish), [[coconut-mung-bean-curry]] (mung bean curry with coconut milk).
